text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are presenting with a chronic cough, weight loss, and generalized weakness. To help me narrow down the cause, have you noticed any fever, night sweats, or coughing up blood recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 68-year-old male. The patient reports having a fever, cough, weakness, night sweats, and poor appetite persisting for 6 months. He has lost 7.5 kg (16.5 lb) over this period. No history of breathlessness, nasal discharge, nasal obstruction, palpitations, chest pain, or digestive symptoms. Released from prison 9 months ago after a 2-year sentence.

speaker: Doctor

The image indicates diffuse infiltrates, which does not match acute appendicitis; given your history of fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, and recent incarceration, this strongly suggests a pulmonary infection. Can you confirm if you have any known history of tuberculosis or other chronic lung diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Chronic cough and fever. I also have Weight loss, Night sweats, Generalized weakness, Poor appetite.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pulmonary Tuberculosis.

The clinical picture of chronic fever, night sweats, significant weight loss, cough, and recent incarceration is classic for reactivation tuberculosis, supported by the chest X-ray findings of diffuse infiltrates. No further tests are required at this time.
